subject: GTA VI on the Windows D3D12 runtime integration

observations.result: The maintainer reports that the Rockstar Games Presents title card now appears.
The reported load reaches the first mission’s intro. The picture stays black and the host GPU fails within seconds. The cause is unresolved.

hardwareForThisRun.scope: Machine identified by the maintainer for the five-stage report.

limitations: The five-stage count describes the scope of this report. PortWatch assigns its own milestones.

interpretation: All selected pipelines in the initial 1404-entry driver-only warm were created, but a later title still rebuilt many.
Persistent-library probes created six, then loaded six with zero new creations. The expensive loads still took about 5-6 seconds each.

timedMemory.interpretation: Independent timer samples, including frame stalls. Byte counters overlap; do not sum them. made_* counters are cumulative, other allocation counters are retained. Missing fields and null pool values are unknown, not zero. Card-side counters may include shared-memory fallbacks.

hostMemory.interpretation: System totals sampled about every five seconds; not attributable solely to Victory. Sampling stalled during pressure. The runner separately observed a smaller commit reserve.

uncappedPhysicalReserve20261125.captureObservation: Frame 1950 is almost black. Frame 2000 shows a partial, dark world with large missing regions. This is not correct or controllable gameplay verification.
uncappedPhysicalReserve20261125.userObservation: User reports gameplay loaded with working audio, fragmented visibility, followed by a crash and system freeze.

windowsEvents.interpretation: WER also reported older LiveKernelEvent dumps from previous dates; their report timestamps do not establish a new GPU reset in this run. The user-observed freeze remains material.

failureSequence: Texture-pool allocation errors began before termination (0x8007000E).
A host compute pipeline was refused for out-of-memory, despite successful shader translation.
A 1 MiB Rust allocation failed and job peak reached the 24 GiB hard limit.
The runner later observed only 44,388,352 bytes of available commit, below its 4 GiB reserve.
All 151 package access paths were restored; AppContainer profile deletion failed with a sharing violation, so launcher exit 125 is a cleanup result.

run.ownershipInterpretation: These independently sampled owner buckets are not exhaustive or atomic. Null means unavailable while a lock was busy, not zero. Retired resource references are not counts of unique leaked resources. Completed submissions still use the unchanged 64-submission quarantine.

videoMemory.interpretation: DXGI process local/shared usage and changing budgets in MiB; not installed capacity or an additional amount to sum with private bytes. Shared usage does not by itself prove VRAM eviction.

run.captureObservation: Private window capture near 65 seconds shows a recognizable character and street, houses, fence, trees and power lines, but very dark rendering. Caption: 2 FPS, 521.7 ms/frame, 2755 draws/frame. Stable gameplay and player response were not verified.

eventLogCheck.limitation: No matching events were found in this interval; absence does not prove driver stability or identify every failure mode.

run.interpretation: Recognizable world geometry is a rendering advance over the preceding dark green/black capture. The run still ended at the job commit notification before scheduled input. lastWorldPreparationBreakdown.interpretation: Overlapping instrumented timings, not additive or a complete GPU-utilization measurement. Light DRED emitted no marker-formatting metric; no quantified marker-formatting speedup is claimed.

changes.result: Implemented per-host-buffer COPY_DEST transition deduplication and bounded, nonblocking retained-owner sampling.
Narrow RGBA32 typed buffer view compatibility fix with authored Radeon semantic coverage; other integer format widths and atomic behavior were not broadly remapped.
Launcher selected existing light DRED breadcrumbs/page-fault reporting without full per-command marker formatting.

windowAliasPrototype.reason: A larger backing can change descriptor logical bounds and alignment-dependent exact-copy decisions. Descriptor-aware bounds preservation is required before this can be treated as a safe memory-only optimization.
